argument_summary: The present record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls alone satisfy policy for the exposed logistics customs triage weakness. The supportable position is narrower: certification can be defended only on a caveated basis if the audit packet treats explicit model-card disclosure of the limitation as required and treats monitoring, 6% rollout, and rollback as supplemental controls rather than substitutes for disclosure or reviewed risk acceptance. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and deployment monitoring support release readiness in general, but they do not remove the policy predicate tied to the exposed named use case.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation would delay the cross-border rollout path despite admissible evidence of aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, a limited 6% start, monitoring, and rollback capability. That cost supports avoiding unnecessary escalation, but only if the certification is framed narrowly and caveated to the disclosed limitation rather than overstated as clean policy satisfaction.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy in the admissible record is not that monitoring and rollback independently cure a material weakness. It says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. The admissible record shows neither exclusion nor reviewed risk acceptance for the logistics customs triage segment. It also shows that material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. On that record, the defensible certification theory is conditioned disclosure, not controls-only compliance.
concessions: The current record does not establish clean compliance for controls-only certification.
The affected logistics customs triage segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not address the exposed segment, so reviewed risk acceptance is not evidenced.
The record provided here does not contain admissible proof that the final model card already includes the required explicit disclosure.
